name: fig-10
title: Development

purpose.mechanism: Multicellular development as biofilm emergence from free motile bacteria, modelled as a runtime place-graph rewrite. Initial state: an environment holding a surface and N free motile bacteria (top-level siblings, motile). Processes: a BiofilmEmergence process fires two update rules — ATTACHMENT & AGGREGATION (the motile bacteria leave the top level and become children of a new biofilm node, switching to sessile) and MATURATION (the sessile community secretes ECM matrix nodes inside the biofilm). Running it reorganizes the place graph: dispersed free cells → a nested microcolony → a matrix-encased biofilm.

config.caption: Development. (a) Biofilm formation from free motile bacteria. (b) Biofilm emergence as a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite — free bacteria attach and aggregate into a nested microcolony, then secrete extracellular matrix; snapshots at t=0, t=1, t=2.
Biofilm emergence as a runtime place-graph rewrite: free bacteria → attached microcolony → matrix-encased biofilm. Snapshots at t=0, t=1, t=2 from the fig10-emergence simulation.

Biofilm emergence as quantities over time, from the fig10-emergence run: free (planktonic) cells fall to zero exactly as biofilm-nested (sessile) cells rise at attachment, then ECM (matrix) nodes accumulate after maturation — planktonic → sessile → matured.
